complexity.notes: Every emitted node costs a scan of up to k heads, so this is O(n*k) = O(n^1.5) on the given ladder; O(n log k) is reachable via ||a min-heap holding one entry per chain head|| or ||recursively merging the k lists in pairs (divide and conquer)||. The short-circuit on equality with the last emitted value is correct because all remaining heads are always >= that value, but with values spread over 0..4n ties are rare, so it almost never fires. Using ListNode(NotImplemented) as the dummy works only because int == NotImplemented happens to be False; a dedicated object() sentinel (or a first-iteration flag) would be clearer than relying on that quirk.
complexity.summary: Filters out empty chains up front, then for each output node rescans every chain head to find the minimum value, short-circuiting the scan when a head equals the last emitted value; the chosen node is spliced onto the result and the input lists are rewired in place.
